newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU ministers seek renewed talks on fur-trap norms.
newsitem.headline: EU ministers seek renewed talks on fur-trap norms.

text.p: European Union foreign ministers told the European Commission on Monday to restart talks with Canada and Russia on international norms for traps used to catch animals for their fur.

Ministers said in a statement that "draft framework agreements with the Russian Federation and with Canada on humane trapping standards, in particular with regard to the conventional steel-jawed leg-hold trap, leave room for improvement on certain points".
Renewed contacts would aim to adapt draft agreements, struck last year, "on the basis of a number of concrete recommendations" made by ministers, the statement said.
The draft deal foresees standards for traps intended to kill or catch 18 species of wild animal, including muskrats, beavers, sable, lynx and wolves.

Commission spokesman Peter Guilford told a news conference the points to be raised included certain trap standards, the possibility of arbitration to reach a final agreement and definitions to be used in derogations for indigenous trappers.

EU environment ministers asked the Commission last December to reopen talks with Canada, Russia and the United States while also preparing the legal texts for a fur import ban to come into force by the end of March if talks failed.

Environment ministers were unhappy that the then deal would ban only steel-jawed, leg-hold traps while leaving less clear the fate of padded traps, whose main difference compared with steel-jawed devices is that their jaws carry rubber strips.

The Commission, led by European Trade Commissioner Sir Leon Brittan, rejected that approach on the grounds that the deal was as good as could be obtained and that a ban risked sparking retaliatory action in the World Trade Organisation.
While Monday's decision rejects Brittan's line, it still means a further delay in solving a problem which has dragged on for years said one EU official, who asked not to be named.
"The whole thing smells like 'postpone it a few more months'," the official said.
